events.title: Counting Butterflies as They Flutter by (Doughton Park - Milepost 238.5)
events.location: Doughton Park located at milepost 238.5 on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Park in the parking lot next to Brinegar Cabin and follow the paved path to the garden.
events.fee: Free
events.description: Be a citizen scientist and help spot and count butterflies as part of the Carolina Butterfly Monitoring Program. thingsToDo.title: Old Rag Circuit
thingsToDo.summary: PARK BOUNDARY | Visitors must obtain an Old Rag day-use ticket in advance of this hike. Pets are not allowed. thingsToDo.title: Stony Man
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 41.7 | Pets are not allowed on this hike. This enjoyable hike brings you to an outstanding view of the Shenandoah Valley, Massanutten Mountain, and beyond.

thingsToDo.title: Whiteoak Falls (Lower)
thingsToDo.summary: PARK BOUNDARY | An easier hike to the base of the lower falls in Whiteoak Canyon. Note that a Park entrance fee is still required.

thingsToDo.title: Spot an Elk on the Heintooga Spur Road
thingsToDo.summary: Heintooga Ridge Road on the southern end of the Blue Ridge Parkway is a good place to spot elk.

thingsToDo.title: Turk Mountain
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 94.1 | A hike to the 2,981’ summit of Turk Mountain, located in the Shenandoah Wilderness, that provides a wonderful view to the west.

thingsToDo.title: Riprap - Wildcat Ridge
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 90 or 92.1 | This loop can be hiked from Riprap Parking or Wildcat Ridge Parking. It takes you through the forests of the Shenandoah Wilderness and over several stream crossings, while offering beautiful views of the hollows and valley to the west and north.

thingsToDo.title: Nicholson Hollow
thingsToDo.summary: PARK BOUNDARY | An alternate option for visitors with pets who still wish to hike from the Old Rag parking area. This hike takes you through the Shenandoah Wilderness to Corbin Cabin, an old homesite built by a former resident, and features several stream crossings along the way.

thingsToDo.title: Knob Mountain - Jeremys Run
thingsToDo.summary: Elkwallow Wayside (mile 24) | This hike goes around a beautiful area of the Park featuring one of the most picturesque streams in Shenandoah. The majority of this hike is in the Shenandoah Wilderness.

thingsToDo.title: Hazel River Falls
thingsToDo.summary: Meadow Spring Parking Area (mile 33.5) | A trail that leads you into the Shenandoah Wilderness to an exceptional waterfall.

thingsToDo.title: Chimney Rock
thingsToDo.summary: Riprap Parking Area (mile 90) | An out-and-back hike into the Shenandoah Wilderness ending at Chimney Rock, an excellent viewpoint with some very interesting geological features.

thingsToDo.title: Cedar Run - Whiteoak Circuit
thingsToDo.summary: Hawksbill Gap Parking Area (mile 45.6) | This hike is very challenging, although those who do it are rewarded with exceptional cascades and waterfalls. You will also hike through the Shenandoah Wilderness along the Cedar Run Trail.

thingsToDo.title: Rose River Falls
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 49.4 | A hike to a dazzling 67' waterfall. For most of this hike, you’ll be on a beautiful trail in the Shenandoah Wilderness.

thingsToDo.title: Overall Run Falls
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 22.2 | A hike into federally designated Wilderness to a view of the highest waterfall in the Park at 93 feet. Unless rain is plentiful, Overall Run Falls may have minimal to no water flow.

thingsToDo.title: Doyles River Falls
thingsToDo.summary: Doyles River Parking Area (mile 81.1) | This beautiful trek takes you along cool, clear mountain streams to two unique waterfalls.

thingsToDo.title: Browns Gap
thingsToDo.summary: Browns Gap Parking Area (mile 83) | This circuit hike leads you to Upper and Lower Doyles River Falls, as well as Jones Run Falls.

thingsToDo.title: Become a Blue Ridge Parkway Junior Ranger
thingsToDo.summary: Becoming a Blue Ridge Parkway Junior Ranger is exciting and rewarding! Pick up your Junior Ranger Folder and instructions at any park visitor center. Then travel the parkway to get site-specific activity sheets along your journey.

thingsToDo.title: Stargaze at Waterrock Knob
thingsToDo.summary: Stargazing on the Blue Ridge Parkway can be an amazing experience. Waterrock Knob at Milepost 451.2 is a great place to enjoy the calm quiet of the night and contemplate the universe as you gaze at the starry sky that surrounds you.

thingsToDo.title: Marys Rock From Meadow Spring
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 33.5 | This alternate route to Marys Rock Summit offers an easier and shorter trek to the same incredible westward views of the Shenandoah Valley. Along the way, hikers will pass by the remnants of the former Meadow Spring Shelter as well as beautiful azalea blooms in season.

thingsToDo.title: Marys Rock Summit
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 31.6 | Many legends surround the name of this hike, but there is no denying the beautiful westward views that it provides of the Shenandoah Valley and Massanutten Mountain.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the Sunrise from Pounding Mill Overlook
thingsToDo.summary: Sunrise on the Blue Ridge Parkway can be an amazing, once-in-a-lifetime experience. Pounding Mill Overlook at Milepost 413 is a great place to welcome the dawn of a new day and appreciate the natural beauty of this special place.

thingsToDo.title: Watch Peregrine Falcons at Devils Courthouse
thingsToDo.summary: Peregrine falcon, once near extinction, now can be viewed in the skies over the Blue Ridge Parkway.

thingsToDo.title: Mill Prong - Laurel Prong Loop
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 52.8 | A circuit hike to Camp Rapidan, the rustic getaway of President Herbert Hoover and First Lady Lou Henry Hoover. Today, this restful spot features exhibits on the First Couple and their perspectives.

thingsToDo.title: Rapidan Camp
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 52.8 | A hike, featuring three stream crossings, to the rustic getaway of President Herbert Hoover and First Lady Lou Henry Hoover. Today, this restful spot features exhibits on the First Couple and their perspectives.

thingsToDo.title: Hawksbill Summit via Upper Hawksbill
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 46.5 | A hike to the top of Shenandoah’s highest peak, offering 360-degree views of the Shenandoah Valley, the Blue Ridge Mountains, and the Virginia Piedmont.

thingsToDo.title: Watch for Hawks at the Mills River Overlook
thingsToDo.summary: The raptors are coming! And they’ve got the “kettle” on!

thingsToDo.title: OVVI Junior Ranger
thingsToDo.summary: Overmountain Victory National Historic Trail Junior Ranger booklet and directions.

thingsToDo.title: Hawksbill Summit
thingsToDo.summary: Hawksbill Gap Parking Area (mile 45.5) | A shorter, yet steeper route to Shenandoah’s highest peak. The viewing platform on top of Hawksbill offers a magnificent 360-degree panoramic view of the Shenandoah Valley, the Blue Ridge Mountains, and the Virginia Piedmont.

thingsToDo.title: Hawksbill Loop
thingsToDo.summary: Hawksbill Gap Parking Area (mile 45.5) | A circuit hike to Shenandoah’s highest peak. The viewing platform on top of Hawksbill offers a magnificent 360-degree view of the Shenandoah Valley, the Blue Ridge Mountains, and the Virginia Piedmont.

thingsToDo.title: Whiteoak Falls (Upper)
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 42.6 | This challenging hike to cascades and waterfalls has been popular since the early days of Skyland Resort. This particular hike goes to the upper falls before returning.

thingsToDo.title: Sugarloaf Loop
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 22 | Follow the trail to a viewpoint. In the early summer, the showy white flowers of mountain laurel bloom in abundance here.

thingsToDo.title: Dark Hollow Falls
thingsToDo.summary: Dark Hollow Falls Parking Area (mile 50.7) | Pets are not allowed on this hike. This hike follows a stream to a beautiful waterfall, and is one of the Park’s most traveled trails. The trail is short, but very steep and rocky and the return hike is challenging!

thingsToDo.title: Compton Peak
thingsToDo.summary: Compton Gap Parking Area (mile 10.4) | A hike through the forest along the Appalachian Trail to a western view and a great look at columnar jointing, an exciting geologic feature.

thingsToDo.title: Appalachian Trail - Tanners Ridge Road
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 52.8 | A fairly level hike that takes you through a former homestead on the famous Appalachian Trail.

thingsToDo.title: Old Rag Summit via Berry Hollow
thingsToDo.summary: Berry Hollow Parking Area (Park Boundary) | Visitors must obtain an Old Rag day-use ticket in advance of this hike. Pets are not allowed. Old Rag is a popular, strenuous hike with sweeping views. This route starts from the Berry Hollow parking area and allows you to get to the summit without having…

thingsToDo.title: Frazier Discovery Trail
thingsToDo.summary: Loft Mountain Wayside (mile 79.5) | Pets are not allowed on this hike. This hike features several picturesque overlooks as it passes through woodlands of varying ages on Loft Mountain.

thingsToDo.title: Save A Bear's Life
thingsToDo.summary: Your actions while visiting the parkway can have a direct and lasting impact on a black bear. Discover how YOU can save a bear's life!

thingsToDo.title: Hawk Watch at Harveys Knob
thingsToDo.summary: Every autumn, thousands of raptors ride the thermal updrafts of the Blue Ridge Mountains on their way to wintering grounds. You can watch the graceful flights of these soaring birds from Harveys Knob Overlook.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Adney Gap
thingsToDo.summary: Take a scenic drive through Adney Gap around milepost 136 and experience one of the many mountain gaps that provided an important early tool in traversing the surrounding hills and mountains.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Tuggle Gap
thingsToDo.summary: Take a scenic drive through Tuggle Gap to experience one of the gaps which provided early travelers passage through the mountains.

thingsToDo.title: Mahogany Rock Overlook
thingsToDo.summary: Visit the Mahogany Rock Overlook for soaring views of Buck Mountain, Doughton Mountain, and Cheek Mountain among others. In the fall visitors are treated to spectacular views of migrating raptors.

thingsToDo.title: Hike the Gully Creek Trail Loop
thingsToDo.summary: While this hike is challenging, the trek is very rewarding for the seasoned hiker. The small cascades are pure magic!

thingsToDo.title: Bicycle the Blue Ridge Parkway
thingsToDo.summary: The Blue Ridge Parkway offers 469 miles of picturesque road cycling though the Virginia and North Carolina mountains.

thingsToDo.title: Enjoy Sunrise at the Afton Overlook
thingsToDo.summary: The Afton Overlook provides an excellent introduction to the Blue Ridge Parkway. The view is spectacular at any time, but the colorful skies produced at sunrise can be truly breathtaking. And remember: No two sunrises are the same. So if you can, plan a few return visits to this unique overlook.

thingsToDo.title: Go Fishing in the Mountains
thingsToDo.summary: A mountaintop park may seem an unlikely place to fish, but just the opposite is true. The parkway protects over 100 miles of streams, many of them small, spring-fed watercourses that rise along the spine of the Blue Ridge. In addition, there are13 artificial lakes along the parkway.

thingsToDo.title: Fox Hollow Trail
thingsToDo.summary: Dickey Ridge Visitor Center (Mile 4.6) | Pets are not allowed on this hike. Discover the cultural history of Shenandoah National Park as you pass by historic rock walls, a cemetery, and periwinkles planted by former residents. This hike is also a designated TRACK Trail, featuring a self-guided…

thingsToDo.title: Limberlost
thingsToDo.summary: Limberlost Parking Area (mile 43) | An ADA accessible path through the forest with mountain laurel in the springtime and an example of a columnar jointing geological feature. This hike is also a designated TRACK Trail, featuring a self-guided brochure designed for kids.

thingsToDo.title: Blackrock Summit
thingsToDo.summary: Blackrock Parking Area (mile 84.4) | A short hike to a viewpoint on top of a rocky talus slope with incredible views of the Shenandoah Valley, Massanutten Mountain, and beyond. This hike is also a designated TRACK Trail, featuring a self-guided brochure designed for kids.

thingsToDo.title: All About Hiking - Start Here!
thingsToDo.summary: With over 500 miles of trails in Shenandoah National Park, chances are high that you'll be lacing up your hiking boots at some point on your next trip here.

thingsToDo.title: Stargaze in Shenandoah
thingsToDo.summary: Shenandoah National Park has distinctly accessible night skies that make stargazing and astrophotography a fun and insightful activity for all ages.

thingsToDo.title: Go Birdwatching in Shenandoah
thingsToDo.summary: Birdwatching is a fun activity that the whole family can enjoy, and Shenandoah provides the perfect habitat to spot a variety of different species, including those colorful, neotropical migratory birds!

thingsToDo.title: Jones Run Falls
thingsToDo.summary: Jones Run Parking Area (mile 84.1) | This hike takes you over a mountain stream, through the forest, and beside a 42’ waterfall.

thingsToDo.title: Hightop Summit
thingsToDo.summary: Hightop Mountain Parking Area (mile 66.7) | Wind your way up a ridge on this hike to a rocky viewpoint that stands at 3,296 feet.

thingsToDo.title: Fort Windham Rocks
thingsToDo.summary: Compton Gap Parking Area (mile 10.4) | A short hike along the Appalachian Trail that leads to an interesting geologic feature.

thingsToDo.title: Hike the Devils Courthouse Trail
thingsToDo.summary: Make the steep 0.5 mile climb to the top of Devils Courthouse for one of the most fantastic views on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Enjoy breath-taking, panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and the valley below from one of the most unique vantage points on the Parkway.

thingsToDo.title: Bearfence Viewpoint
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 56.4 | Pets are not allowed on this hike. This route takes you to a 180-degree view of the Shenandoah Valley without a rock scramble.

thingsToDo.title: See the Rhododendrons Bloom at Craggy Gardens
thingsToDo.summary: Colorful rhododendron blossoms put on a show each summer along the Blue Ridge Parkway and one of the best places to see these high-elevation flowers is at Craggy Gardens.

thingsToDo.title: Traces Trail
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 22.2 | A hike that follows a trail around Mathews Arm Campground. Along the way, you’ll see traces left behind by former residents of the area.

thingsToDo.title: Story of the Forest
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 51 | Pets are not allowed on this hike. An easier stroll through the woods that passes next to the Big Meadows Air Quality Station, an important place for scientists and researchers to learn about air quality in Shenandoah.

thingsToDo.title: South River Falls Observation Point
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 62.7 | From the South River Picnic Grounds, this hike leads you through a verdant forest alive with a wide variety of plant and animal life to a stone-walled observation point overlooking an 83’ waterfall.

thingsToDo.title: Snead Farm Loop
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 5.1 | Hike through old apple orchards and farmlands to an historic barn on the former Snead homesite.

thingsToDo.title: Pass Mountain Loop
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 31.6 | A hike along the Appalachian Trail to a shelter. Be on the lookout for wildflowers and birds through the fairly open woods along the trail!

thingsToDo.title: Millers Head
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 42.5 | From the Skyland amphitheater, take this hike to a spectacular viewpoint at the site of a former fire tower.

thingsToDo.title: Lands Run Falls
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 9.2 | A short hike down a fire road to a series of cascades that descend about 80 feet into a gorge. Note that it may not have water in dry seasons.

thingsToDo.title: Bearfence Rock Scramble
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 56.4 | Pets are not allowed on this hike. An exhilarating rock scramble leads to a magnificent 360-degree view of the Virginia Piedmont and Shenandoah Valley.

thingsToDo.title: South River Falls
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 62.7 | From the South River Picnic Grounds, this route is a circuit hike that takes you to an observation point overlooking an 83’ waterfall. A great hike for wildflower and bird enthusiasts, alike!

thingsToDo.title: Little Devils Stairs Loop
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 19.4 | A journey into a rocky gorge with some very rewarding, yet steep, sections along a stream.

thingsToDo.title: Lewis Falls Trail
thingsToDo.summary: MILE 51.2 | Leaving from Big Meadows amphitheater, this hike leads to an observation point over a beautiful 81’ waterfall.

thingsToDo.title: Look for Migrating Monarch Butterflies
thingsToDo.summary: Among the fall wildflowers, and drifting on invisible wind currents high above you, look for the jewel tones of monarch butterflies as the insects pass through the parkway's high elevations on their seasonal migration.

thingsToDo.title: Hike the Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center Loop Trail
thingsToDo.summary: The Blue Ridge Parkway Visitor Center Loop Trail is a short, easy hike that is popular with all ages. Locals and visitors alike enjoy this leg stretcher trail and its close proximity to Asheville.

thingsToDo.title: Hike the High Meadow Trail at the Blue Ridge Music Center
thingsToDo.summary: A hike on the family-friendly High Meadows Trail leads up and down rolling grassy meadows and through a mix of deciduous and evergreen forests. Pick up some Kids In Park TRACK Trail brochures at the trailhead to add adventure to your kid's hike. The trail provides a quiet retreat with limited…

thingsToDo.title: Hike the Roanoke River Trail
thingsToDo.summary: The ideal hike for someone who likes water, bridges, woods—and doesn’t feel like committing an entire afternoon to a hike. Roanoke River Trail is an an easy trail that covers less than a mile. It makes a perfect leg stretcher hike as you pass through Roanoke.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the Sunrise at Pine Tree Overlook
thingsToDo.summary: There are many places to view a sunrise along the Blue Ridge Parkway, but the sun rising over the Peaks of Otter at Pine Tree Overlook is a stand out favorite on the northern end of the parkway.

thingsToDo.title: Hike to Rattlesnake Lodge
thingsToDo.summary: Step back in time with a hike to historic Rattlesnake Lodge. This enjoyable hike through shaded woodlands is close to Asheville and takes you to the remains of an early1900’s mountain retreat.

thingsToDo.title: Spend the Night in the Mount Pisgah Campground
thingsToDo.summary: The Mount Pisgah Campground is a cool, high elevation retreat in the summer's heat. This peaceful and relaxing spot is the perfect place to stay and explore the southern end of the Blue Ridge Parkway.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Middle Prong Wilderness
thingsToDo.summary: Want to take a walk on the wild side? Try a hike in the Middle Prong Wilderness! Adjacent to the Blue Ridge Parkway, this wilderness area protects a beautiful forest and has ample opportunities for solitude.

tours.description: What makes a mountain? Is it more than just the rocks underfoot? This hike is a 1.6 mile circuit up to the summit of Stony Man Mountain and back down. Classified as "easy" Stony Man does have a total ascent of 340 feet. Hikers will tour past features, both natural and historic, and take a closer glimpse at the building blocks that make this mountain. Fascinating geology, everchanging trees and…

tours.title: Big Meadows Civilian Conservation Corps Camp
tours.description: Shenandoah National Park hosted 11 Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) Camps between 1933 and 1941. The CCC was a popular New Deal Program designed to put young men and women to work during the Great Depression. One of the camps was established at Big Meadows (mile 51).
